thread: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: [1] RE: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase
body:
Information Governance Team,

*Case Ref 00210772 — internal review requested 7 July 2026*

Thank you for your email of 11 September. You said that you would try to
update me by the end of the following week with a clearer timeframe. I have
not received that update.

Under regulation 11(4) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004,
an internal review should be completed as soon as possible and no later
than 40 working days after receipt of the request for reconsideration. On
my calculation, that period expired on 2 September 2026. The review is
therefore now overdue.

I appreciate that further historical documentation has been located and
that you may need to consult third parties. I am not asking you to
compromise any proper consultation process. However, I ask that you now
provide the following by *Tuesday 6 October 2026*:

1. *A firm date* by which the completed internal review decision will be
issued.

2. *A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located*,
including, so far as presently known:
- its approximate date or date range;
- who created or supplied it;
- how it came into the Council's possession; and
- approximately how many documents are involved.

I am asking for a description of the material and its provenance, rather
than disclosure of its substantive contents.

3. *Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved in
its present form*, without alteration, destruction or disposal, while
the internal review and any subsequent complaint to the Information
Commissioner remain outstanding.

4. *Release now of any material that can properly be disclosed without
awaiting third-party consultation*, where the Council has already
established that no exemption or other restriction prevents disclosure.

If I do not receive a substantive response by *6 October 2026*, I will
refer the continuing delay to the Information Commissioner's Office without
further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: EIR 00210772 — internal review and formal chases
subject: Re: Great House Farm, Llandough – Request 00210772 – Internal Review – Formal Chase – unanswered points from 30 September and 11 September
body:
Information Governance Team
cc: Monitoring Officer; Data Protection Officer

Case Ref 00210772 — Internal Review requested 7 July 2026

This is a formal chase of unanswered points already put to you. It is not a new request and must not be used to restart any clock.

On 11 September 2026 you wrote that service areas had found further historical documentation, that you were still sifting it, and that because some of it is “not necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council’s possession” you were considering whether to consult third parties. You said you would try to give a clearer timetable by the end of the following week (i.e. by 18 September 2026).

On 30 September 2026 I asked, by Tuesday 6 October 2026, for:
1. A firm date by which the completed internal review decision will be issued;
2. A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located (date range, creator/supplier, how it came into the Council’s possession, approximate volume);
3. Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved without alteration, destruction or disposal; and
4. Immediate release of any material that can properly be disclosed without awaiting third-party consultation.

None of those four points has been answered.

What you have not said
You have not identified a single document found in the September sift. You have not named any third-party consultee class, the date any consultation was sent, or the date by which a reply was required. You have not stated whether the material is held under EIR or FOIA. You have not addressed the child / personal-data point previously raised. You have not confirmed a preservation hold. Silence on each of these points is itself a recorded position.

What is now required (unchanged from the unanswered requests)
(a) Issue the internal review decision. On any view the ICO’s recommended maximum of 40 working days from the request for review (7 July 2026) has long passed. If you contend that EIR does not apply, say so expressly and identify the statutory basis for treating the request under FOIA alone.

(b) Attach a schedule of every document found in the further search: date, description, format, holding service, whether Council or third-party record in the Council’s possession, and the decision on each (disclose / part-disclose / withhold with the precise regulation or section).

(c) If any third-party consultation has occurred or is proposed, name the class of consultee, the date the consultation was sent, and the deadline set for reply. A consultee’s silence is not a ground to withhold.

(d) Confirm in writing that every document in the sift, and every related planning, enforcement, legal, committee, land, finance and correspondence record (including predecessor-authority material), is under a formal preservation hold and will not be destroyed, weeded, transferred or disposed of while 00210772 and related requests remain open.

(e) Address the child / personal-data point: if any record has been withheld or is being considered for withholding because it mentions a child, identify the record and the exemption. If no such withholding exists, say so expressly. Treat the personal-data element also as a subject-access request under UK GDPR for Sion Hywel Buckler (child occupant in 1988).

The 7 July 2026 answer treated the matter as a planning-register query. That was too narrow. The sift must cover the full list previously set out (planning files including unpublished appendices, enforcement, building control, environmental health, demolition, legal-services files, member/officer correspondence, land/estates files, finance records, and predecessor-authority transfers to Glamorgan Archives).

Public-accountability questions (to be answered from the documents, including those found in September)
1. Was any Council or predecessor expenditure, fee, cost, grant or works associated with the occupation, demolition or redevelopment?
2. Was any Council or predecessor land, right, permission or undertaking involved?
3. Were officers or members told of anything that contradicted or qualified the ownership, occupation, heritage or demolition account then being used?
4. What accounting, audit, legal, planning, committee and correspondence records survive?
5. Was any irregularity, conflict, material error or control failure identified, reported, or formally accounted for?
6. If the Council’s position is that there is nothing to examine, state that expressly and identify the documents relied on.

By return
Within 5 working days: the document schedule, the preservation confirmation, and either the child-exemption notice or a clear statement that none exists.
Within 10 working days: the internal review decision with copies of everything you are able to disclose.

This email records that the four points put to you on 30 September 2026 remain unanswered as of 6 October 2026. If no substantive response is received, the continuing failure to complete the internal review will be referred to the Information Commissioner without further notice.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

Information Governance Team,

I refer to the internal review of Case Ref 00210772 (Great House Farm / Ty
Mawr, Llandough) which I requested on 7 July 2026.

On 5 August 2026 you acknowledged that the matter remained outstanding
beyond the 20-working-day statutory period and stated that further
enquiries with service areas were ongoing. You indicated a further update
or decision would be provided.

As of the close of business on Friday 14 August 2026 no substantive
response or decision has been received.

This is a formal chase. The Environmental Information Regulations 2004
require that internal reviews be completed promptly and, in any event,
within a reasonable time. The delay is now significant.

Please provide the completed internal review decision within 5 working days
of this email (i.e. by close of business on Monday 24 August 2026).

If a full response is not received by that date I may escalate the matter
to the Information Commissioner’s Office for non-compliance with the
statutory timescales under the EIR, which I do not care to do.

Please also confirm, as part of the outstanding review or by way of further
disclosure under the same reference:

1. Whether the Council (as local planning authority) considered issuing a
Building Preservation Notice under section 58 of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1971 (or any equivalent provision) in respect of Great House
Farm at any time between July and December 1988.

2. If it was considered, who decided against it and on what grounds.

3. If it was not considered, why not, given that the building was under
active bailiff enforcement, partial demolition of outbuildings had already
occurred, and Cadw had publicly stated on 3 December 1988 that listing was
under active consideration.

A Building Preservation Notice would have provided interim protection at
the critical moment. Its absence is material to the internal review of the
original response and to the wider handling of the case.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergenant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
Williams/ Buckler Family Estate

body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for information about Great House Farm, Williams/Buckler Family, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan and the further clarification that was received on the 7th June. Your request has been processed under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004.

The Council's Planning records have been reviewed and the Planning department has provided the following response:

In line with your clarification that was received on the 7th June, searches have been undertaken by the Council's Planning department in relation to the historic Great House Farm / Ty Mawr estate in Llandough. This includes land adjacent to and including Church View Close and the north side of Leckwith Road, with particular reference to the area identified within Land Registry title WA231076 and the timeframe indicated from 1875 onwards, where records exist.

We have been advised that the links to the planning records relating to the redevelopment of the site during the 1980s-1990s have previously been provided by colleagues in the Planning department. These records, including associated documentation, are publicly available via the Council's Planning Register and can be accessed using the relevant application reference numbers at View or Comment on a Planning Application.
This information is therefore excepted under Regulation 6(1)(b) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 - information already publicly available and easily accessible by other means.

Whilst planning files may contain some archaeological information, it is also noted that archaeological records for the Vale of Glamorgan are maintained by Heneb (formerly Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust). We suggest that you contact Heneb directly to access relevant records. Details on how to contact them can be found at Heneb - The Trust for Welsh Archaeology. To the extent that the Council does not hold further archaeological reports beyond those contained within planning files, Regulation 12(4)(a) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (information not held) applies.

Following searches of Planning records, no additional information has been identified within the scope of your request. You asked whether any records may have been transferred to Glamorgan Archives or otherwise. It is possible that historic material of this nature may be held externally, and you may therefore wish to contact Glamorgan Archives directly. Details on how to contact them can be found at https://glamarchives.gov.uk/contact/.

From the clarification provided, the Council has been unable to identify which specific GIS datasets are being sought. Please provide further clarification regarding this and once received, we will consider this element further.

As previously advised, the Council does not hold records relating to the legal case of BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. Neither the Vale of Glamorgan Council nor its predecessor authorities were parties to that case, which appears to have been a private legal matter. Accordingly, information relating to those proceedings is not held by the Council.

If you are dissatisfied with the handling of your request, you have the right to ask for an internal review. Internal review requests should be made within 40 working days of the date of receipt of the response to your original letter and should be addressed to:
c/o The Monitoring Officer - Foiunit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
Or by post to The Monitoring Officer, Civic Offices, Holton Road, Barry, CF63 4RU.

If you are not content with the outcome of the internal review, you have the right to apply directly to the Information Commissioner for a decision.

subject: Re: EIR/FOI request - 00210772 (Great House Farm / Church View Close, Llandough) – Further Clarification and Request for Full Disclosure
body:
FOI Unit / Evelyn Morgan / Information Governance Team,

Thank you for your email dated 2 June 2026 and for the assistance provided
so far in relation to reference 00210772.

I appreciate the Council's efforts to support this important family matter
and note your confirmation that no records are held regarding the private
legal proceedings in *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler*.

As background, this case related to the longstanding claims of my
Williams/Buckler family to ownership of Great House Farm (Ty Mawr). My
grandmother Mary Williams maintained until her conveniently timed death in
1983 (in the 2 week window to challenge BP's registration of our home and
land since 1667, in their names) that our family held ownership of the
house following arrangements with Daniel Thomas involving the quarry, with
the surrounding farmland subject to a lease that defaulted.

There was a conveyance for the surrounding land and attempt to merge our
farmhouse and garden into that single plot in 1975. Which was challenged by
my nan. Something HM Land Registry correspondence (titles WA231076 and
WA240304, first registered to BP Properties Limited in 1982/1983)
references these conveyances and the Court of Appeal decision, which may
assist in narrowing relevant planning and heritage searches.

To enable your Planning, Heritage, and other relevant teams to conduct
thorough searches without further delay, I confirm that enquiries should
cover the historic Great House Farm / Ty Mawr estate in Llandough (adjacent
to and including areas now known as Church View Close, north side of
Leckwith Road, title WA231076). This includes any planning permissions,
heritage assessments, demolition records (circa 1988), tenancy notations,
environmental information, or correspondence from 1875 onwards.

I am keen to receive a full and timely response within the statutory
timeframe, drawing on all information the Council holds across departments.
This is of profound personal and historic importance to the Williams family
descendants as we seek to document and substantiate our family's position.
Should any records have been transferred to Glamorgan Archives or handled
in any other way, details of this would be most helpful.

Thank you once again for your understanding and support in this sensitive
matter. I look forward to your substantive reply at the earliest
opportunity.

Kind regards,

*Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sergeant)* bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz [redacted] (On behalf of the Williams / Buckler family
descendants)

Delivery-failure notices were returned for foi@museumwales.ac.uk, Cadw@gov.wales and askthearchives@cardiff.gov.uk.
body:
LEGAL NOTICE TO RECIPIENTS:
*Take notice that this request is issued in anticipation of formal legal
proceedings and the filing of an official report regarding systemic
institutional fraud, land misconduct, and the unlawful concealment of
historic preservation data. You are under a strict legal duty to preserve
all physical and electronic records, metadata, correspondence, maps, and
erased files relating to this site. Any spoliation, deletion, or
withholding of data will be cited in subsequent court filings.*
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,
RE: Information Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004
I am writing to request access to historical records, internal
correspondence, planning briefs, and assessments held by your organization
regarding Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth/Cardiff (demolished
December 1988), and the historical occupancy of the Buckler family.
Statutory Mandate on Accessibility & Charging Fees:
I am aware that previous attempts to locate this data have resulted in
directives to visit physical archives in person or use paywalled,
commercial third-party web portals. Please be advised of the following
statutory obligations:

   1. Under EIR Regulation 8, fees cannot act as an unreasonable barrier or
   deterrent to access. Because my family was historically displaced from this
   site and I am executing this request remotely, forcing physical attendance
   or demanding payment constitutes an unlawful obstacle.
   2. Public authorities are required to supply information in the format
   requested. I require all documents to be delivered digitally via email
   attachment or secure electronic download link, free of charge, as
   specified by the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) guidelines for
   data already held electronically.

Please provide all recorded information matching the following points:
1. Tenant/Ownership Identification and the 1880 Report

   - Any documents, archival notes, or registry indexes citing the
William/ Buckler
   family line (who occupied and farmed the house across four generations).
   - Clarification on whether my family members were formally cited as the
   legal owners, long-term tenants, or registered reporters of the 1880
   discovery under the dining room floor.
   - Any explicit records indicating gaps, deleted metadata, or missing
   volumes in your authority’s archive concerning the tenancy, land-dispute
   maps, or agricultural heritage of Great House Farm between 1950 and 1989.

2. Statutory Protection and Cadw’s Assessments

   - Given that the site's extreme archaeological value (a
   1st-to-4th-century Roman precursor villa and a massive early medieval
   monastic settlement) was verified by rescue operations as early as 1979,
   what are the recorded reasons why Cadw failed to place a statutory
   Schedule or Protection Order on the standing fabric of Great House Farm
   before its demolition?
   - All internal correspondence, risk assessments, or ministerial briefs
   evaluating the preservation value of the sub-medieval direct-entry
   farmhouse core before it was levelled.

3. Planning Approvals and Local Authority Governance

   - All minutes, planning committee files, and consultation responses from
   the local authority that granted planning permission and housing
   development rights on this specific acreage.
   - Direct information explaining how the council approved planning
   permission for a private housing development in light of the documented
   historical evidence surrounding the immediate parish boundary.

4. Institutional Concealment and Historical "Ignorance"

   - Records showing exactly where and at what stage of the planning
   process this archaeological evidence should have been brought up
but was not,
   which ultimately allowed developers and public bodies to claim they were
   unaware of the land's deep significance until after the farmhouse was
   destroyed and housing development began.
   - Any environmental impact assessments, historic environment register
   (HER) lookups, or developer briefs filed between 1980 and 1990 regarding
   the footprint of Great House Farm.

If any part of this request is refused under the guise of commercial
sensitivity or archival limitations, you are required by law to state the
exact statutory exemption applied and provide a formal internal review
pathway.
I expect your response within the statutory 20-working-day timeframe.
Kind regards,
*Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)*

body:
Dear Mr Buckler

The Council's Information Governance Team works collaboratively, and requests are managed collectively across the team rather than by individual officers. For this reason, correspondence is not issued under individual names. The team is managed by Evelyn Morgan who is the Council's Data Protection Officer/Information Manager.

We appreciate the detailed correspondence you have provided to date and understand that this matter is of importance to you. We have received multiple items of correspondence from you, including earlier requests relating to the legal case of BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. Work had already been undertaken to review this request and we were in the process of preparing a response when your more recent correspondence was received. We were aiming to ensure that all appropriate lines of enquiry had been explored before providing a response.

At this stage, we would like to clarify that the Vale of Glamorgan Council does not hold records relating to this historic legal matter. Neither the Council nor its predecessor authorities, the Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council or the former South Glamorgan County Council were involved in the case of BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. From the information available, it appears this was a private legal matter between BP Properties Ltd and the Buckler family. We also recognise that your enquiries extend beyond the Council and have been shared with a number of organisations. Some of the information you are seeking is more likely to be held elsewhere and not with the Council. Some information that may have historically been retained by the Council may now be held by the Glamorgan Archives but only in relation to historical land ownership, tenancy records, or court administrative deposits. Some information may also be obtainable from the Land Registry, but we can see that they have been included in your correspondence.

In terms of information the Council may hold, this is most likely limited to planning related records. As previously advised, in order for our Planning colleagues to conduct accurate searches, they have requested a copy of the relevant site plan. Without this, there is a risk that any searches undertaken may not capture all relevant records. We note that this does not mean there are records just that in trying to cover every possibility we have asked for a site plan to complete this aspect of our enquiries. There may not be anything held but, we are trying to search for you. It is entirely a matter for you as to whether you provide a site plan. If you do not wish to provide one you do not have to but that will restrict our enquiries as it will be difficult to pin down the correct area.

We are looking to assist in providing you with a full response as soon as possible with the information that is held by the Council. Your cooperation in providing the requested plan will help us progress this matter efficiently.

We look forward to hearing from you.

to: planning@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk (cc pcu@levellingup.gov.uk, enquiries@homesengland.gov.uk, enquiries@planninginspectorate.gov.uk, defra.helpline@defra.gov.uk, PEDW.Casework@gov.wales; bcc c1v@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk)
subject: BP v Buckler 1987 and the 1982 land registration of Great House Farm, Llandough (now Church View Close)
note: No reply from the Council appears in this thread.
body:
Sirs/Ma'am,

I'm writing in relation to land formerly known as *Great House Farm,
Llandough (Vale of Glamorgan)*, subsequently developed for residential use
and historically connected with the proceedings culminating in *BP v
Buckler (Court of Appeal, 1987)*.

I appreciate that the Local Planning Authority is not responsible for
determining land ownership, nor am I asking it to do so. My purpose is to
place on record a *chronological summary of unresolved land-governance
issues* which may be material to the integrity of the planning history
relied upon for that site.

In brief and as reflected in public records:

- In *July 1974*, proceedings involving my grandmother and BP both
asserting ownership, were adjourned and did not result in a judicial final
determination.

- On *31 October 1974*, a further listed hearing did not proceed
substantively, following correspondence sent that morning by BP entities.
No judgment on title was issued. My nan requested the audience with the
judge the day before, with her lawyer. But that got leaked, the press
descended on our farm (not that I can find evidence of news articles from
said press), and the following morning the two letters from BP arrived to
our solicitor, effectively squashing the court hearing and audience with
the judge my nan had sought, to make her case of ownership. Her reply to
both BP letters (one from BP Pension Trust Ltd and one from BP Properties
Ltd), that morning of the 31st of October, was also 'I own the land'.

- Throughout this period, my grandmother was *excluded from dealings*
concerning land we asserted we owned, while the opposing party
continued to *assert
ownership*, notwithstanding the absence of a concluded judicial finding.

- In or around *1982*, the land was registered in BP’s name, despite the
earlier proceedings never having resolved the competing claims nor having
resulted in findings adverse to my grandmother.

- My grandmother then died in *1983*, after the registration had taken
place, without compensation and without any final adjudication of her claim.

- In the *1987 appeal*, the Court referred to correspondence as having
been replied to (albeit not to the correct corporate entity - which is
ultimately why we lost BP vs Buckler 1987), yet in my fathers appeal that
followed, whereby he argued that surely BP Pension Trust should have been
the claimant not BP Properties, the same judge from the case dismissed the
appeal citing that both companies were effectively the same. This is all
evidence on the face of the public record of these proceedings.

- By that stage, and in the absence of a documentary title which had
effectively been overtaken by registration, my family was driven to advance
arguments in adverse possession as a *fallback position*, which itself
should have assured our continued occupancy.

The cumulative effect was that my family was *displaced*, the land was
developed, and no compensation was ever paid, despite ownership never
having been conclusively decided in court. Whether intentionally or not,
the process operated in a manner where asserted ownership became treated as
settled fact.

I am not alleging misconduct, nor am I seeking retrospective remedies from
the Authority. I am simply asking whether, given the above sequence, it
would be appropriate for the Authority to:

- note that historic planning decisions were taken on the basis of *assumed
title*, and

- record that the underlying ownership dispute was *never finally
adjudicated*, for the sake of transparency and future governance
integrity.

This correspondence is intended to be factual, measured, and
non-adversarial. I am happy to supply references to the relevant hearings,
registrations, or judgments if that assists your records. But what I'm
highlighting here is all on public record and in the public eye.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler

body:
Information Governance Team
Vale of Glamorgan Council
FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
cc: planning@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

New request under FOIA 2000 and/or EIR 2004. Do not treat this as a reopening or expansion of 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484. Those cases stay as they are.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Leckwith Road, Llandough, later Church View Close.
Applications: 89/01396/OUT (outline granted 13 March 1990) and 92/00671/RES.

I already have, or have already asked for, the officer's report, Policy H.2 text, Appendices C–E, the decision notices, and the general archaeological-condition papers. This request is confined to classes that those earlier requests did not name.

Please disclose recorded information held, or confirm item by item if not held:

1. Section 52 / later section 106 / land charges
Any agreement under section 52 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971, any later section 106 instrument, any deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding entry on the local land charges register. Search legal, planning and land-charges holdings, not only the 2026 planning-file scan. If none is held, say so expressly. That is an open records question, not a conclusion that none existed.

2. Historic planning register
The planning-register entries that the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 required the authority to keep for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES: the applications, reserved-matters applications, plans and drawings, and relevant decision information. If the 2026 file disclosure is incomplete against that register, say what the register still lists and what is missing from the file.

3. Appendix B
Appendix B to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT: the further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust. Case 00211463 asked for C, D and E and for a list of annexes. It did not ask for B by that description. If B is not held, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and whether any copy survives elsewhere.

4. Condition 16–18 chain
Named papers, not a general search:
(a) conditions 16, 17 and 18 as issued on the 13 March 1990 permission;
(b) the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17;
(c) GGAT's archaeological warning of July 1992;
(d) the September 1992 reserved-matters approval, and whether any further archaeological condition was attached;
(e) the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters recommending a breach-of-condition notice.

5. Environmental assessment / screening
Any preliminary environmental-assessment determination, screening opinion, or recorded decision that an environmental statement was or was not required for 89/01396/OUT. The application site is described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 hectares. I am not asserting that an environmental statement was required. I am asking whether the Council made and recorded the determination at all.

6. Archaeological-interest consultation route
Any record of the statutory consultation route actually used because the land was recorded in the county Sites and Monuments Record, or was treated as a "site of archaeological interest" under the 1988 Order. I am not asking you to treat SMR status as automatic proof of a particular duty. I am asking what route was used.

7. Application receipt date
The Council's receipt record for 89/01396/OUT. The application form is dated October 1989. The reconstructed planning record gives 8 November 1989 as receipt of the application and plans. Please supply the date-stamped receipt, validation or register entry.

8. 92/00671/RES completeness and applicant standing
(a) A file list or register for 92/00671/RES showing what the reserved-matters file originally contained.
(b) Any sale, option, conditional-contract or authority-to-apply paper on the planning files covering the change from BP Properties (1989 outline applicant) to Ideal Homes Wales (appearing on the 1992 reserved-matters trail), including the recorded BP-to-Ideal Homes transfer of 3 December 1993.
This is a documentary interest/authority question. It is not an allegation that the 1992 application was invalid.

If a record is not held, say so for that item. If it was destroyed, transferred or archived, give the date, the schedule, and any surviving catalogue. Search planning, legal, land charges and archived/scanned holdings.

Please give a new reference and the 20 working-day date. Preserve anything in scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . I am not asking the Council to decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

body:
Freedom of Information Officer,

Case Ref: 00211463 — request received 17 September 2026

I write to clarify and refine the above request while it remains open,
having now examined the original manuscript of the planning officer's
report rather than a transcription. My earlier request named two
organisations; the document in fact identifies the correspondents
differently, and I ask that the request be read as follows.

The passage relied upon
The planning officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT (residential
development including new access road, land at Great House Farm, Leckwith
Road, Llandough, Penarth; outline permission granted 13 March 1990) states,
at page 2:

"Two letters have been received from the Barry Preservation Society and
Civic Trust and a local County Councillor (who is a member of the Glamorgan
Gwent Archaeological Trust) making representations in respect of this
application and a copy of both these letters are attached to this report as
Appendices 'C' and 'D' respectively."

The following paragraph of the same report states:

"The Applicants' Agents have written in response to the report of the
Glamorgan Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd. on the site and a copy of this
letter is attached to this report as Appendix 'E'."

What I request
Appendix "C" to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT — the letter from the
Barry Preservation Society and Civic Trust.

Appendix "D" — the letter from the local County Councillor referred to,
together with that Councillor's name.

Appendix "E" — the letter from the Applicants' Agents responding to the
report of the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd.

A list of all appendices ("A" to "E" or further) to that officer's report,
so that the complete annex set is identified.

Any register, index, schedule or file list for application 89/01396/OUT
recording the documents originally held on the file.
A further document referred to in the same report

The officer's report also records, of the East Vale Local Plan:

"The greater part of the land is allocated for new residential development
in the East Vale Local Plan (Policy No. H.2.) The information supporting
the policy states that buildings on the site should be retained, however
were unfortunately demolished a little while ago."

I therefore also request:
The text of Policy H.2 of the East Vale Local Plan and the supporting
information to that policy referred to above, in the version current in
1989–1990.

Points on handling
These are documents the Council's own report states were attached to it. If
any of them is not held, I ask the Council to say so expressly, and to
state (a) when it ceased to be held, (b) under what retention schedule or
disposal decision, and (c) whether any record of that disposal exists. A
response that "no additional information has been identified" would not
address a request for annexes that the Council's own report records as
attached.

I note the Council's letter of 11 September 2026 in a related matter, which
stated that "further historical documentation has been found... not
necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council's
possession". I ask that this material be searched in responding to the
present request.

I intend this as a clarification and refinement of case 00211463 under the
Council's duty to advise and assist (s.16 FOIA 2000 / reg. 9 EIR 2004), and
not as a new request. If the Council takes the view that any part of it
must be treated as a fresh request, please confirm that in writing,
identify which parts, and give the revised due date, so that I am not left
uncertain which deadline applies to which element.
I should be grateful for confirmation of receipt.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

subject: Great House Farm, Llandough (89/01396/OUT)
body:
Dear FOI Unit,

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and/or the Environmental
Information Regulations 2004 (whichever regime the Council considers
applicable to the material), I am requesting information held in relation
to:

- Planning application *89/01396/OUT* (outline permission granted 13
March 1990); and
- The subsequent reserved matters application *92/00671/RES*,

both concerning land at Great House Farm, Leckwith Road, Llandough,
subsequently developed as Church View Close.

I am seeking to reconstruct the documentary planning and consultation
record between the outline permission and the subsequent
detailed/reserved-matters approval.
1. Consultation responses to application 89/01396/OUT

The Council's own case officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT
records, in its consultations section:

"Cardiff Bay Development Corporation: No objections – however, the
Corporation would hope that the trees on the slope of the site facing
north-west are retained and that the public right of way which runs through
the site will be retained."

The same report refers to further consultation responses from the *National
Rivers Authority* and the *County Engineer* by reference to attached typed
sheets ("please type attached sh②" and "please type attached sh③"), without
reproducing their substantive contents in the disclosed copy.

Please therefore provide:

1. The *complete original written response from the Cardiff Bay Development
Corporation* concerning application 89/01396/OUT, including any
accompanying letter, report, plan, attachment or other document forming
part of that consultation response.

2. The *complete National Rivers Authority consultation response* referred
to in the report as one of the attached sheets, including the original
document and any accompanying material.

3. The *complete County Engineer consultation response* referred to in the
report as one of the attached sheets, including the original document and
any accompanying material.

I am deliberately not relying upon the handwritten numbering of sheets ②
and ③ to identify which sheet belongs to which consultee, as the numerals
are difficult to distinguish in the surviving copy. Please identify the
corresponding sheet/document by reference to its contents or file
provenance.

4. Any *covering correspondence, transmission record or internal record*
showing when the NRA and County Engineer responses were received by the
Council and how those responses were placed on, incorporated into or
considered as part of the planning file.

2. Archaeological assessment and discharge of outline conditions

Please provide:

5. The *formal decision notice and complete schedule of conditions* issued
in connection with planning application 89/01396/OUT, including any
condition concerning archaeological investigation, evaluation, assessment,
excavation, recording, preservation or protection.

6. All records held by the Council demonstrating the *discharge,
implementation or consideration of any archaeological condition*
attached to the 1990 outline permission, including any archaeological
evaluation, field assessment, report, correspondence, approval, discharge
notice, consultation response or internal officer record.

7. Any correspondence or documentation showing how the Council considered
the findings of that archaeological work in determining the subsequent
reserved matters application 92/00671/RES.

3. Reserved matters application 92/00671/RES

Please provide:

8. The *formal decision notice* for application 92/00671/RES, including the
complete schedule of any conditions attached to the approval.

9. The consultation responses and representations received in connection
with 92/00671/RES, including any response or representation from
the *Cardiff
Bay Development Corporation*, if one exists.

10. Any officer report, committee report, delegated report, recommendation
or internal planning assessment relating to the determination of
92/00671/RES.

11. Any document recording the Council's consideration of the relationship
between the reserved-matters proposal and the parameters established by the
outline permission 89/01396/OUT.

4. Change from the outline scheme to the reserved-matters scheme

The officer's report for the outline application describes the indicative
scheme as *18 dwellings*, whereas the subsequent reserved-matters scheme
appears to comprise *20 dwellings*.

Please therefore provide:

12. Any document held by the Council recording or explaining the change from
the indicative *18-dwelling* scheme at outline stage to the *20-dwelling*
scheme submitted/approved at reserved-matters stage.

13. Any planning assessment, officer report, correspondence,
committee/delegated report or other record explaining the planning basis
upon which the additional two dwellings were considered acceptable under
the outline permission.

14. Any document identifying the relevant condition, parameter, planning
provision or other mechanism under application 89/01396/OUT under which the
reserved-matters scheme was considered capable of differing from the
indicative 18-dwelling layout.

5. Scope and record availability

For the avoidance of doubt, this is *not a request for a general search of
all historic records concerning Great House Farm*. It is specifically
directed to the planning records and decision-making documents identified
above for applications *89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES*.

Please search the relevant planning application files and associated
archived/scanned material, including attachments and documents stored
separately from the principal application file where those documents form
part of the application or consultation record.

Please supply the information electronically, such as scanned copies, where
practicable.

If any requested record is *not held*, please confirm this specifically for
the relevant item rather than leaving the point unanswered.

If the Council considers that any information is exempt from disclosure,
please identify the *specific exemption or exception relied upon* and
explain its application.

If any of the identified historical records were previously held but are no
longer available, please confirm, where recorded:

- whether the record was destroyed, transferred, archived elsewhere or
otherwise disposed of;
- the date or approximate date of that action, if recorded;
- the authority or process under which it occurred; and
- whether any surviving catalogue, disposal schedule, transfer record or
other audit trail exists.

I also understand that the application for housing began much further back
as a petition was made in 1974 for 13 houses. Please could you give me a
reference or link or that entire planning application record too.

Please acknowledge receipt of this request and provide a reference number.

I understand that the statutory response period is 20 working days.

Regards,

thread: FOI/EIR 00211463 — planning appendices C, D, E and Policy H.2 (89/01396/OUT)
subject: FAO: Barry Preservation Society / the Civic Trust
body:
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,

I am researching the 1989 planning application for the development
subsequently known as Church View Close, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

The planning officer's report records that representations were received
from the *Barry Preservation Society* and the *Civic Trust*, but the report
does not reproduce the substance of those representations.

Please provide copies of all records held by the Council relating to the
representation made by the *Barry Preservation Society* in connection with
that planning application, including:

1. The original letter, objection or representation submitted by the
Barry Preservation Society.
2. Any covering letter, acknowledgement or correspondence concerning its
submission.
3. Any internal Council correspondence referring to or summarising the
Society's representations.
4. Any plans, photographs or supporting material submitted by the
Society.
5. Any correspondence concerning the *retention, preservation,
alteration or demolition of Great House Farm farmhouse*.
6. Any subsequent correspondence between the Council and the Barry
Preservation Society concerning Great House Farm or the development.

I am particularly seeking the Society's *original 1989 comments about Great
House Farm farmhouse*, rather than a later summary of them.

The organisation is referred to in later Vale of Glamorgan Council records
as the *Barry Preservation Society*, including its participation in the
Council's Conservation Area Advisory Group. It also appears in historical
publications as the *Barry Preservation Society and Civic Trust*.

If the original representation is no longer held, please state that
explicitly and provide any surviving reference, file number, minute,
extract or other record that identifies what was submitted and when.

Please search the complete planning file and associated correspondence
rather than relying solely on the published officer report.

Regards,

Sion Buckler

thread: FOI/EIR 00211027 — acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School
from: Information Governance Officer, Vale of Glamorgan Council (FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk)
subject: FOI request - Case Ref/ 00211027
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for information about Llandough Primary School and your further enquires around whom you within the Information Governance team you have been corresponding with.

You asked

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, I request copies of records relating to the acquisition of the land used for the construction of Llandough Primary School.

Specifically, I request:

■ The transfer deed, conveyance or other legal instrument by which the Council acquired the land.

■ The purchase price or consideration paid for the land.

■ If the land was gifted, transferred at nominal value or below market value, records explaining the basis for that arrangement.

■ Any valuation reports obtained before acquisition.

■ Any agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP (or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company) concerning the transfer of the land.

■ Any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports authorising the acquisition.

■ Any planning agreements or obligations connected with the transfer.

If any of the requested information is already publicly available, please provide the relevant links or document references.

You then issued further correspondence requesting:

On 14 July 2026 you acknowledged my FOI/EIR request (Case Ref 00211027) concerning the acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School.

I replied the same day asking for the name of the officer who sent the acknowledgement. I have received no further response or substantive reply.

Our Response

The transfer deed, conveyance or other legal instrument by which the Council acquired the land
The Council holds a conveyance dated 11 June 1965 made between:
1. Lakeside and Llandough Development Company Limited;
2. Western Ground Rents Limited; and
3. The Glamorgan County Council.
A scanned copy of the conveyance and its plan is attached (“the 1965 Conveyance”).

The purchase price or consideration paid for the land
The consideration recorded in the 1965 Conveyance is £16,800.

If the land was gifted, transferred at nominal value or below market value, records explaining the basis of that arrangement
The 1965 Conveyance records a purchase for £16,800. No record has been located within the papers held by Legal Services indicating that the land was gifted or transferred at nominal value or below market value.

Any valuation reports obtained before acquisition
Searches were undertaken with Legal Services and Estates Department. No valuation report relating to the acquisition has been identified. The Council does not hold any valuation report falling within the scope of this request.

Any agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP, or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company, concerning the transfer
No agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and BP or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company relating to the acquisition of the land have been identified.

Any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports authorising the acquisition
The Council has not identified any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports within its current records management systems which fall within the scope of your request. Given the age of the acquisition, any surviving historic records may have been transferred to Glamorgan Archives. You may wish to contact Glamorgan Archives directly regarding records from this period.

Any planning agreements or obligations connected with the transfer
No planning agreement or planning obligation connected with the 1965 Conveyance has been identified within the title deeds held by Legal Services or, within the Planning Departments records.

We have considered this aspect of your correspondence under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.
The Council’s Information Governance Team deal with requests on a collective basis and all requests will be considered by different officers. The requests are dealt with via a generic e-mail account so that all officers in the Team can consider correspondence. There are several reasons why the Information Governance Team work in this way. One reason is to ensure that correspondence is considered as soon as possible and to ensure that messages or e-mails are not sent to individuals and overlooked within our systems overall. The information requested is also considered to constitute the personal data of a member of staff and disclosure would amount to disclosure to the world at large. Therefore the Council is unable to provide the name of the individual officer, because it is not considered that there is a lawful basis that would make disclosure fair or necessary in the circumstances. The Council's correspondence is issued on behalf of the authority, and requests for information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 or the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 are made to the Council as a public authority rather than to individual officers. It is not necessary to know the identity of a particular officer in order to submit a valid request for information.
If you are dissatisfied with the handling of your request, you have the right to ask for an internal review. Internal review requests should be made within 40 working days of the date of receipt of the response to your original letter and should be addressed to:
c/o The Monitoring Officer – Foiunit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Or by post to The Monitoring Officer, Civic Offices, Holton Road, Barry, CF63 4RU.
